NoteTexAccessor::math_funcs¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch NoteTexAccessor::math_funcs() const

Recognize Function Commands Inside Math¶

math_funcs() extracts the names of recognized mathematical function control words from complete math fragments. The current vocabulary is sin, cos, tan, log, ln, exp, max, min, argmax, argmin, det, Pr, and sqrt. Tokens omit the leading backslash: \sin contributes "sin".

Only content inside $...$, $$...$$, \(...\), or \[...\] is searched. The same words in prose are ignored, as are escaped dollar signs and incomplete math regions. Matching is case-sensitive and requires a complete control-word boundary, so a longer custom command is not classified by prefix. This is a lexical classifier, not expression evaluation: it does not infer that f(x) is a function or validate argument arity.

Results preserve source order and repetition. They use TokenBatch offsets to retain cell ownership while flattening variable token counts. Undefined input propagates as undefined tokens; non-text input is rejected. Runtime is linear in scanned bytes plus recognized tokens.

Example 1: Functions Across Four Math Delimiters¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{
        R"(prose 99; $x_1 + \sin(\alpha) = 2.5$)",
        R"(\[\beta \leq y^2\] and \(\sqrt{z}\))",
        R"(escaped \$7 and plain theta)",
        R"($$\argmax_x f(x) \approx 10$$)"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto result = source.tex().math_funcs();
std::cout << result.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["sin", "sqrt"]

Example 2: Cell Ownership¶

const auto offsets = result.offsets().integers();
for (auto value : offsets) std::cout << value << ' ';
std::cout << '\n';

Output¶

0 1 2 2 2

\argmax_x is one longer control word, not the exact built-in \argmax, so the boundary rule excludes it.

Example 3: Undefined Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().math_funcs().tokens().defined()
          << '\n';

Output¶

false

See Also¶

  • ids: return all ASCII identifier lexemes, including command names.

  • symbols: retain complete control words with their backslashes.

  • sqrt_pow: transform roots instead of classifying them.
